context:
Goal: one uniform direction for every watch, wake, sweep and reap (your item 180).
Problem (rule): decision the-janitor-is-one-machine-wide-sweep and janitor/GUIDE.md say the sweep never runs code a repository supplies. But sweep.py's repo reaper (run_repo_reaper) runs an npm script from each repo. The record and the code disagree.
Based on (read): lane watchers-prose-and-plan, 07:51 CST, read janitor/sweep.py on main.
Departs from: main (record says no repo code runs; code runs it) — a: the record allows the repo reaper by name; b: the reaper is removed.

Meanwhile: #1228 merges without it, and the reaper stays as it is.

options.gain: Per-repo cleanup keeps working; the record tells the truth.
options.how: Amend the record: only your own repos, only their named cleanup script. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.
options.label: Keep the reaper, and allow it by name in the record (coordinator reading)
options.lose: An unattended sweep runs repo code, so a bad script in one repo runs with no one watching.

options.gain: The sweep runs only its own code, as its record says.
options.how: Delete run_repo_reaper from sweep.py; each repo runs its own cleanup inside its own work.
options.label: Remove the reaper
options.lose: Each repo's own cleanup must run some other way, or not at all.

ref: item 180; docs/plans/align-watchers.md Q7; claude-settings #1228; lane watchers-prose-and-plan
title: Should the janitor keep running each repo's npm cleanup script?
why: Withdrawn 07:59 CST: already decided. Your ruling uniform-over-variants (2026-10-27 12:51 CDT) says a shared tool never grows a per-repo exception, so the janitor's repo reaper goes (option b). The coordinator files it in the align-watchers plan.
